tour.overview:
An hour west of Doha, the peninsula of Zekreet is one of the emptiest and most striking landscapes in the Gulf: a plain of pale gravel and sand, broken by limestone escarpments and rocks that the wind has carved into mushrooms and tables, ending in low cliffs above a calm sea. In 2014 the American sculptor Richard Serra placed one of his largest works here, East-West/West-East – four steel plates, each more than 14 metres tall, standing in a straight line across a kilometre of desert in the Brouq Nature Reserve.

This private tour in a 4x4 takes you to the sculpture and the landscape around it with a local guide. You walk between the plates, which line up with the two rocky ridges on either side of the valley and change colour with the light, then drive across the reserve to the mushroom rocks and to Film City, a mock Arabian village built as a film set and now standing alone among the rocks. On the way back you stop at the coast for a last view over the water. The sunset departure is especially beautiful, when the steel and the rocks turn red.

AT A GLANCE
• Duration: about 5 hours (morning or afternoon/sunset)
• Start and finish: your hotel in Doha
• Distance: about 180 km round trip, partly on desert tracks
• Type: private 4x4 with an English-speaking guide-driver
• Booking: on request – we confirm availability and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay only then
• Activity level: easy, short walks on uneven ground

WHAT YOU SEE
• Richard Serra's East-West/West-East.
• The Brouq Nature Reserve and its limestone escarpments.
• The mushroom rocks of Zekreet.
• Film City.
• The west coast near Zekreet.

WHY THIS TOUR WORKS
The sculpture and the rock formations are reached by sand and gravel tracks without signs, and the best photographs depend on the time of day. A private 4x4 with a guide who knows the tracks gets you there safely and at the right light, without the dune bashing of a safari.

WHO WILL ENJOY IT
Art and architecture lovers, photographers, families, and anyone who wants to see a quieter, wilder side of Qatar in half a day.

WHO MIGHT PREFER ANOTHER TOUR
For high dunes and the sea in the desert, choose our desert safari to the Inland Sea. For history and heritage, our North Qatar day trip visits the UNESCO site of Al Zubarah.

PRACTICAL INFORMATION
Wear closed shoes for the rocky ground, a hat and sunglasses. There are no shops or toilets in the reserve: water is provided in the car. In summer choose the late-afternoon departure.

days.name: West Qatar Tour
days.description:
What to expect: a private half day in a 4x4 on the Zekreet peninsula – Richard Serra's East-West/West-East, the Brouq Nature Reserve, the mushroom rocks and Film City.

Your guide-driver collects you from your hotel and takes the Dukhan highway west across the peninsula. After about an hour you leave the tarmac for the gravel tracks of the Brouq Nature Reserve, a protected area of limestone escarpments, sand and sparse desert plants where you may see gazelles and, in spring, flowering shrubs.

The first stop is East-West/West-East by Richard Serra, unveiled in 2014: four rolled-steel plates, each more than 14 metres high, set in a straight line about a kilometre long across a valley between two rocky ridges. The plates are placed so that their tops align with the ridges, and their rusted surface changes from brown to deep red with the light. You can walk the full line or simply stand between the plates and feel their scale against the empty landscape.

From the sculpture the 4x4 crosses the reserve to the mushroom rocks of Zekreet, limestone pillars whose softer base has been worn away by wind and sand, leaving heavy caps balanced on thin stems – a favourite subject for photographers. Nearby stands Film City, a small mock Arabian village with towers and courtyards built as a film set, now strange and silent in the desert. Before heading back to Doha you stop at the coast near Zekreet, where low cliffs look over a shallow, turquoise sea.

SCHEDULE (times are estimates; sunset departure in brackets)
07:30 (13:30) – Pick-up at your hotel in Doha.
08:45 (14:45) – Brouq Nature Reserve and East-West/West-East (about 45 minutes).
09:45 (15:45) – Mushroom rocks of Zekreet (about 30 minutes).
10:30 (16:30) – Film City (about 20 minutes).
11:00 (17:00) – West coast viewpoint (sunset in the afternoon).
12:30 (18:30) – Return to your hotel.

GOOD TO KNOW
• There are no shops, cafés or toilets in the reserve; we carry water and soft drinks.
• Access to parts of the reserve can occasionally be restricted; your guide adapts the route.
• This tour can be combined with the desert safari or the North Qatar day trip on consecutive days.

INCLUDED: private 4x4 and guide-driver, water and soft drinks, hotel pick-up.
NOT INCLUDED: meals, tips.

faq.question: How does booking on request work?
faq.answer: You choose your date, morning or sunset, and the number of travellers and send the request. Nothing is charged. We confirm availability and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay online only once your tour is confirmed.

faq.question: Is there dune bashing on this tour?
faq.answer: No. The 4x4 is needed for the gravel and sand tracks, but the drive is calm. For dune bashing, choose our desert safari to the Inland Sea.

faq.question: What is East-West/West-East?
faq.answer: A sculpture by the American artist Richard Serra, unveiled in 2014: four steel plates, each over 14 metres tall, standing in a line about a kilometre long in the Brouq Nature Reserve. It is one of the largest works of land art in the region.

faq.question: Morning or sunset?
faq.answer: Both work. The morning is cooler; the late afternoon gives warm light on the steel and the rocks and a sunset over the west coast, which most photographers prefer.

faq.question: How far is it from Doha?
faq.answer: About 80 to 90 km, roughly an hour each way, plus the drive inside the reserve on gravel tracks.

faq.question: Is the tour private?
faq.answer: Yes. The 4x4 and guide-driver are for you and your group only, so you can stay longer wherever you like.

faq.question: Are there entrance fees?
faq.answer: No. The sculpture, the reserve, the mushroom rocks and Film City are free to visit.

faq.question: Is it suitable for children and older travellers?
faq.answer: Yes. The drive is gentle and the walks are short, though the ground is uneven in places. Child seats are available on request.

faq.question: What should I wear?
faq.answer: Closed shoes for the rocky ground, light clothes, a hat and sunglasses. In winter, a light jacket for the evening.

faq.question: Can we combine it with other tours?
faq.answer: Yes. Many travellers combine it with the desert safari or the North Qatar day trip. We can also build a full day covering the west and the north.

faq.question: Can we fly a drone?
faq.answer: Drones need a permit in Qatar and are not allowed everywhere. Please check the current rules before bringing one.

faq.question: When is the best time of year?
faq.answer: October to April. In summer the tour is best started in the late afternoon to avoid the midday heat.

faq.question: What is your cancellation policy?
faq.answer: You can cancel free of charge up to 24 hours before the tour. Before your request is confirmed, nothing is charged at all.
